newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Chan to meet Chinese premier Li Peng.
newsitem.headline: HK's Chan to meet Chinese premier Li Peng.

text.p: Hong Kong's Chief Secretary Anson Chan said on Wednesday she would voice the concerns of Hong Kong people when she meets Chinese leaders in Beijing this week.
But Chan would not be drawn on whether she would raise the thorny question of civil liberties.

"I will, of course, be discussing with Chinese leaders a range of transitional issues and I will take this opportunity to reflect to leaders any concerns that Hong Kong people may have," Chan told reporters after returning from an official visit to Thailand.
Chan, the popular and influential head of the civil service and deputy to British Governor Chris Patten, will accompany Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa on a visit to Beijing on Thursday.
Chan, who will remain in her post and become Tung's second-in-command, said she would meet Chinese Premier Li Peng and China's top policy maker on Hong Kong, Lu Ping.
When pressed by reporters on whether she would bring up human rights issues during the talks, Chan replied she would be discussing a range of transitional issues with Chinese leaders.
Hong Kong, a British colony for more than 150 years, reverts to China at midnight on June 30.

The territory of 6.4 million people has been promised it can maintain its capitalistic way of life and freedoms for 50 years after the handover but Beijing's plans to repeal certain clauses in its civil liberties laws have raised concerns, particularly in the pro-democracy camp.
